captures.notes: Verified programmatically: 4 records parse, every pointer resolves BACKWARD, every RDLENGTH matches the bytes emitted, TXT strings exactly fill RDLENGTH, total consumed = 127 = len(packet). Legal values I chose rather than lifting from one specific capture: instance label "nexaprint", port 80, address 192.168.1.42, TXT contents. Deliberate structural hazards: (a) 0xc046 at offset 111 points into ANOTHER record's RDATA, which is legal and is what Apple mDNSResponder emits — it kills any 'compression = dictionary of previously-emitted record owner-names' shortcut; (b) 0xc017 at offset 80 points at a SUFFIX (offset 23, mid-name), so pointer targets are not name starts; (c) the cache-flush bit is 0 on the shared PTR and 1 on the three unique records, so the class word is not a constant. Honest RFC caveat: RFC 2782 says the SRV target field is not compressed in unicast DNS; RFC 6762 §18.14 permits compression in mDNS rdata for the known compressible types and real mDNS responders do compress SRV targets. I compressed it deliberately because that is the harder and more realistic mDNS case.

statefulness:
mDNS is connectionless, so §5's connect/login/authenticated skeleton is the wrong shape entirely — yet mDNS is MORE stateful than a session protocol, not less. What it needs from the state model:

(1) LEGAL-MESSAGE-PER-STATE — a responder has a genuine lifecycle: probing -> announcing -> established -> (conflict) -> renaming -> probing. RFC 6762 §8.1: before claiming a name you MUST send 3 probe queries (qtype ANY, 250 ms apart, from the same source address). Announcements are legal ONLY after probing completes with no conflict; an authoritative response for a name you have not probed is a protocol violation. This maps well onto validIn/requires: "mdnsResponsePtr": { "validIn":["announcing","established"], "requires":["probe"] }. What does NOT map is the transition trigger — see (4).

(2) MANDATED CHAINING — probe(x3) then announce(x2, 1 s apart, RFC 6762 §8.3) then serve. §5's "requires":["probe"] expresses "probe succeeded earlier" but cannot express "probe succeeded THREE TIMES, at 250 ms spacing, with no conflicting response in between". The step graph's loop:{max:n} counts iterations but carries no inter-packet timing contract and no "and nothing contradicted you during the window" predicate. A probe that gets no answer is success-by-silence, which is the inverse of §4's expect/timeout polarity: here TIMEOUT is the success edge and MATCH is the failure edge. That inversion is expressible (edges carry on:"timeout") but it is not what the confirmed/presumed vocabulary is built for.

(3) MUTUAL EXCLUSION — conflicts:["firmwareUpdate"] is the right primitive but mDNS needs it against ITSELF: while probing you must not answer authoritatively for the name being probed; simultaneous-probe tiebreaking (§8.2, lexicographic rdata comparison) means two hosts probing the same name enter a comparison that one must lose. "conflicts" is a session-scoped never-combine; this is a state-scoped mutual exclusion between a message and a state, which is already covered by validIn. The genuinely missing piece is the tiebreak: the losing side is decided by comparing YOUR rdata against THEIRS byte-wise — a decision rule over a decoded peer message with no home in §5.

(4) STATE DISCOVERED FROM UNSOLICITED TRAFFIC — this is the biggest structural mismatch. §5's "implies" hangs off an expect step, i.e. off a reply to something you sent. In mDNS you learn your state is wrong from a packet nobody solicited: another host multicasts an authoritative record for the name you believe you own, and you must immediately drop to renaming. There is no preceding send to attach implies to. The model needs a standing observer that is live in every state and can drive transitions with no request in flight. Same mechanism is needed for goodbye packets (TTL=0) and for duplicate-question suppression (if another host multicasts your pending question within the window you must cancel your own send — you are reacting to traffic addressed to nobody).

(5) CONFIRMED vs PRESUMED — mDNS makes this explicit on the wire, and §5 is close but scoped wrong. Every received record is a fact with a TTL, so "presumed until re-confirmed" is native. The cache-flush bit (0x8001) means "my answer supersedes everything else you hold for this name/type — but delete the old entries after 1 second, not immediately" (RFC 6762 §10.2), which is a two-stage confidence decay. TTL=0 (goodbye) is an explicit invalidation. RFC 6762 §5.2 requires refresh queries at 80/85/90/95% of TTL: a record is confirmed at receipt and decays to presumed as it ages. §5's effects.presume/confidence/ttl is per-MESSAGE ("after setRelay we presume the relay is on"); here the presumption is per-DECODED-RECORD, N of them per packet, each with its own TTL and its own flush semantics. The model has no per-capture-element fact emission.

(6) NEGOTIATED CAPABILITY — listed as a known gap in §5 and mDNS hits it twice. The QU bit (query class bit 15) REQUESTS a unicast response; the responder decides, and may answer by multicast anyway. And known-answer suppression means a response may legitimately contain FEWER records than the question covers, because the querier declared what it already knows. In both cases you get less than you asked for and that is success, not partial failure.

(7) SEQUENCE / WINDOW / RATE — no sequence numbers (the DNS ID is 0 and carries nothing), but hard rate rules that behave like a window: at most 1 query per second per question, exponentially backing off to 60 minutes; responses delayed 20-120 ms randomly for shared records to avoid collision; duplicate-answer suppression if you see someone else answer within 500 ms. None of this is expressible; there is no minInterval, no jitter, no dedup window.

(8) FRAGMENTATION — the TC bit means the known-answer list continues in a follow-up packet 400-500 ms later, so ONE logical query spans multiple UDP datagrams. That is exactly the fragmentation/reassembly gap §5 admits to, and mDNS needs it in the SEND direction as well as receive.

(9) MODAL RE-ENCODING — a legacy unicast query (source port != 5353) forces a DIFFERENT encoding of the same logical response: the question MUST be echoed back, TTLs MUST be capped at 10 s, the response goes unicast to the source port. Same message name, two byte layouts, chosen by a property of the peer. §5 has no per-state message variants.

(10) CORRELATION — §4 offers socket | token | broadcast. mDNS fits none cleanly. There is no token (ID is 0), the socket is a shared multicast group, and while "broadcast" correctly yields a list, correlation must be done by matching each response's record NAME and TYPE against the outstanding question, because the response carries no question section at all (QDCOUNT=0, verified in my capture). Correlation is a predicate over decoded records, and responses for one logical query keep arriving indefinitely from new devices — there is no completion, only quiescence.

gaps.what: No field kind can decode a length-prefixed, self-terminating label sequence — not even an UNCOMPRESSED DNS name. v0 has no way to read N bytes where N was just read from the stream.
gaps.why: Query offsets 12..29: `05 5f 68 74 74 70 04 5f 74 63 70 05 6c 6f 63 61 6c 00`. To decode this you must read u8=5, then consume 5 bytes, then repeat until 0x00. `{"skip":2}` takes an integer LITERAL per §3. `{"each":"expr"}` needs a count known in advance; the label count is only known when 0x00 is reached and there is no `until`. `{"tlv":{"t":"u8","l":"u8"}}` is the only length-driven read in v0 and it mandates a leading type byte — a DNS label is L-V, not T-L-V. This blocks decode of every DNS name in both packets, before compression is even considered.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a `name` field kind that subsumes labels, terminator, backpointer, compression choice and the hop guard in one construct:
{ "name": { "encoding":"dnsLabels",
            "unit":{ "len":"u8", "max":63 },
            "terminator":"00",
            "backref":{ "marker":{"mask":"c0","match":"c0"},
                        "offsetBits":14, "base":"message",
                        "direction":"backward", "maxHops":16 },
            "maxDecodedLen":255,
            "separator":"." },
  "value":"inputs.service",   // encode
  "as":"qname",               // decode
  "compress":"auto|never|always" }
Encode with compress:auto consults the engine offset table (see the engine gap); compress:never emits the full sequence. This single field kind fixes 4 of the 5 blockers below.

gaps.what: 0xC0 compression pointers carry an ABSOLUTE offset into the whole message. Encode cannot compute one (no offsetOf), and decode cannot follow one (no seek, no message base, no cursor save/restore).
gaps.why: Response offset 111 is `c0 46` = pointer to absolute offset 70. Offset 70 is not a field, not a group boundary, and not any name the document declares — it is a byte position that happens to fall INSIDE the SRV record's RDATA. Offset 80 is `c0 17` = 23, which points at the SUFFIX `local` halfway through the first record's owner name. So even a hypothetical offsetOf(group:X) is insufficient: targets are arbitrary interior byte positions. On encode I was forced to write five `{"const":"c0 xx"}` literals computed by hand; they are correct only while inputs.service encodes to exactly 18 bytes and the instance label to exactly 9. Change either and the packet is silently corrupt with no validation error. On decode, following `c0 46` requires random access to the whole received buffer, so decode is provably not a forward fold over a cursor.
gaps.proposedFix:
Give the engine a message-scoped name/offset table plus absolute addressing, exposed to the grammar only through the `name` field kind:
ENCODE: while emitting, the engine records (fullyQualifiedName -> absoluteOffset) for every name AND every proper suffix of it, as offsets are assigned left to right. `compress:"auto"` emits the longest suffix match as a 2-byte pointer.
DECODE: the decoder is handed `message.base` + `message.length`, and `name` resolution seeks absolutely, bounded by backref.maxHops and backref.direction:"backward" (reject forward pointers), then restores the saved cursor.
Also add to "limits": { "maxNameHops":16, "maxDecodedNameLen":255, "maxMessageBytes":9000 }.

gaps.what: §3's two-pass model — "pass 1 emits a placeholder OF THE DECLARED WIDTH" — is unsatisfiable for compression, because the width of a compressed name depends on its own byte offset, which depends on the widths of everything before it. That is a genuine cycle in the encoder model, not just a missing feature.
gaps.why: The SRV target at offset 70 is 12 bytes when compressed (`09 nexaprint c0 17`) and 17 bytes uncompressed. Which one is emitted depends on whether `local` already appeared at a reachable offset, i.e. on the byte position of everything before it. RDLENGTH at offset 62 is 18 vs 23 accordingly, and record 3's owner name offset, and record 4's pointer target 0x46, all shift. §3 promises "a cyclic span dependency is a validation error, never a runtime failure" — under that rule this document is rejected at validate time, so the encoder never runs at all. Measured cost of the ambiguity: my semantically identical response is 127 bytes compressed and 215 bytes uncompressed.
gaps.proposedFix:
Split the two passes by concern instead of by field:
Pass A (layout): walk fields left to right assigning absolute offsets. Any field may declare "widthDependsOnPosition": true (set implicitly by `name` with compress:auto); such a field is RESOLVED during pass A, in order, because everything it can reference is already behind it. Backward-only pointers make this terminating by construction.
Pass B (backpatch): resolve len(group:X) / len(from:A to:B) / checksum over the now-final layout.
Declare the validation rule as: a cycle is an error only if a span expression reads FORWARD of a position-dependent field. That keeps the "no runtime failure" guarantee while admitting compression.

gaps.what: No bounded sub-parse. RDATA must be parsed strictly within RDLENGTH bytes, and `skip` accepts only an integer literal.
gaps.why: Response offset 92 declares rdlength=17 and the TXT strings at 94..110 exactly fill it. A decoder that reads character-strings without the region bound runs straight into the next record's owner name at 111. This is the classic DNS parser over-read class of bug, and v0 cannot express the bound: `{"skip":"capture.rdlength"}` is not sanctioned (§3 shows `{"skip":2}`), and there is no construct that says "parse these fields, consuming exactly N bytes".
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a `region` field kind that bounds a nested field list and, on encode, back-patches its own length:
{ "region": { "length":"capture.rdlength" },   // decode: hard bound, error on over/under-read
  "fields": [ ... ], "as":"rdata" }
{ "region": { "lengthField":"u16be", "includesSelf":false },
  "fields": [ ... ] }                            // encode: emits the u16be length itself
Also: state generally that anywhere §3 shows an integer literal (`skip`, `repeat`, `pad.to`, `each`), an expression is admissible.

gaps.what: No discriminated union. RDATA shape is a function of the TYPE field read two fields earlier, and there is no switch.
gaps.why: In one packet, offset 40 rdata is a name, offset 64 rdata is u16+u16+u16+name, offset 94 rdata is a list of character-strings, offset 123 rdata is 4 raw bytes. Only `when` exists, so this must be faked as N mutually-exclusive `when` fields — which forces every RR type into one flat field list, makes the capture namespace collide across branches, and gives no default arm for unknown types (RFC 3597 requires unknown rdata be retained opaquely).
gaps.proposedFix:
{ "switch":"capture.type", "as":"rdata", "cases": {
    "12": [ { "name":{...}, "as":"ptrTarget" } ],
    "33": [ { "u16be":null,"as":"priority" }, { "u16be":null,"as":"weight" },
            { "u16be":null,"as":"port" }, { "name":{...}, "as":"target" } ],
    "16": [ { "value":null, "conv":"undnsCharStrings", "as":"txt" } ],
    "1":  [ { "value":null, "len":4, "conv":"ipv4", "as":"address" } ] },
  "default": [ { "raw":true, "as":"opaque" } ] }
Nested inside the `region` above so every arm is length-bounded. Encode uses the same block, selecting the arm by the encode-side value of the discriminant.

gaps.what: encode(decode(bytes)) can never be byte-stable, because compression is a free encoder choice and the decoded capture set discards it. This is an inherent property of the protocol, not only of v0 — but v0 has no mechanism to preserve it either.
gaps.why: My 127-byte response and a 215-byte fully-uncompressed one carry IDENTICAL semantics. Record 4's owner name alone has three legal encodings: `c0 46` (2 bytes, points into another record's rdata — what Bonjour emits), `09 nexaprint c0 17` (12 bytes), `09 nexaprint 05 local 00` (17 bytes). Decoding all three yields the same capture "nexaprint.local", so re-encoding cannot recover which was on the wire. Further canonical ambiguities in this one packet: record order within the Additional section is unconstrained; the Answer/Additional split is the responder's choice; TTLs 4500/120 are policy; the cache-flush bit is per-record policy; the query's QU bit is optional; the DNS ID is 0 only by mDNS convention.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a general `raw` capture attribute to EVERY field, giving verbatim on-wire bytes alongside the interpreted value, and let encode replay them:
  decode: { "name":{...}, "as":"qname", "raw":"qnameBytes" }
  encode: { "raw":"capture.qnameBytes" }        // verbatim, no re-derivation
Then declare the round-trip contract at two tiers in §7 and require documents to state which they claim:
  "roundTrip": "semantic"  — decode(encode(x)) == x  (achievable here)
  "roundTrip": "octet"     — encode(decode(b)) == b  (achievable ONLY via raw)
This generalises to every protocol with optional compression, optional padding, or non-minimal integer encodings.

gaps.what: The `dnsName` converter always appends the 0x00 root label, so it cannot produce the partial (unterminated) name that always precedes a compression pointer.
gaps.why: Response offsets 40..49 are `09 nexaprint` with NO terminator, immediately followed by `c0 0c`. `"inputs.instance | dnsName"` yields `09 6e 65 78 61 70 72 69 6e 74 00` — an extra 0x00 that produces the wrong 13-byte sequence `09 nexaprint 00 c0 0c`. There is no clean way to strip a trailing byte either: `drop(n)`/`take(n)` operate from the front, so removing the last byte needs arithmetic on a piped length. I worked around it with `{"u8":"inputs.instance | ascii | len"}` + `{"value":"inputs.instance | ascii"}`, which also assumes `len` returns Int from Bytes — implied by §6 but never stated.
gaps.proposedFix:
Parameterise the converter and add a symmetric tail-trim:
  dnsName(absolute)   -> labels + 00      (current behaviour, the default)
  dnsName(relative)   -> labels, no root terminator
  undnsName(relative) -> inverse
Plus a general `dropLast(n)` / `takeLast(n)` in the bytes group, which is independently useful. Explicitly declare `len : Bytes|Text|List -> Int` in §6's converter kind table.

gaps.what: Section counts must be hard-coded. There is no count()/len() over a List, so a data-driven record set cannot fill QDCOUNT/ANCOUNT/NSCOUNT/ARCOUNT.
gaps.why: Response offsets 6 and 10 carry ANCOUNT=1 and ARCOUNT=3. In my document these are `{"u16be":"1"}` and `{"u16be":"3"}` — literals. If the records came from `{"each":"inputs.records", ...}` the counts could not be derived: §6 lists `len` only in the bytes converter group, over Bytes. So the header and the body can disagree with no validation error, which is exactly the class of bug DNS parsers are hardened against.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add `count` to §6 (List -> Int) and define `len` over List as an alias, then allow it in a span expression the same way len(group:X) works:
  { "u16be": "count(group:answers)" }      // number of `each` iterations in that group
  { "u16be": "inputs.records | count" }
Both resolve in the existing pass-B backpatch, so no engine change is needed.

gaps.what: TXT RDATA is a sequence of u8-length-prefixed character-strings with no type byte and no terminator, filling the region. `tlvList` is the nearest construct and it mandates a type byte.
gaps.why: Response offsets 94..110: `09 "txtvers=1" 06 "path=/"` — pure L-V, repeated until RDLENGTH is exhausted. `{"tlvList":{"t":"u8","l":"u8","items":...}}` would emit a spurious type octet before each string. I had to unroll to a fixed arity of two, so a 3-entry TXT record needs a different document. Same shape recurs across protocols (Bluetooth AD structures, Pascal-string lists, HTTP/2 literal headers).

gaps.what: `bits` is undefined for groups wider than 8 bits, for cross-byte bit order, and for decode mode entirely.
gaps.why: The DNS flags word at offset 2 is 16 bits split 1/4/1/1/1/1/3/4. §3's only example sums to 8 (1+3+4) and every decode example uses whole scalars, so I cannot tell whether a 16-bit `bits` group is legal, whether it is MSB-first across the pair, or whether sub-fields may carry `as:` on decode. The same question kills the cleaner encoding of the QU bit (1+15) at query offset 32 and the cache-flush bit at response offsets 56/86/115 — I fell back to `{"u16be":"0x8001"}`, which fuses a semantic flag into an opaque integer and loses it on decode.
gaps.proposedFix:
Specify `bits` normatively: entries are packed MSB-first, the group MUST total a multiple of 8, a single entry may span up to 32 bits, and on decode each entry accepts `as:`. Add an explicit `width` for readability and validation:
{ "bits": { "width":16 }, "of":[
    {"n":1,"value":"inputs.qu","as":"qu"},
    {"n":15,"value":"consts.CLASS_IN","as":"class"} ] }

gaps.what: Expression semantics are under-specified where decode most needs them: arithmetic beyond `/`, and the meaning of `capture.*` inside an `each` frame.
gaps.why: I need `{"each":"capture.ancount + capture.nscount + capture.arcount"}` to walk the RR sections as one list — §3 evidences only `capture.byteCount / 2`, so `+` may not exist. And inside that `each`, the `switch` on RDATA must read `capture.type` from the CURRENT iteration while the count came from the OUTER frame; §6 defines the `capture.*` path but never its scoping under `each`. With the wrong binding, every record decodes as whatever type the last-parsed record had.
gaps.proposedFix: State in §6: (a) arithmetic `+ - * / %` and comparison/boolean operators are available and bind tighter than `|`; (b) inside an `each`, `capture.*` resolves against the current iteration frame, `capture.^.*` walks one frame outward (repeatable), and `capture.$.*` addresses the message root. Add a validate-time error for an unresolvable capture path so scoping mistakes are caught statically, consistent with §6's converter type-checking promise.

gaps.what: §4's expect-correlation kinds (socket | token | broadcast) cannot correlate an mDNS response to its query.
gaps.why: §4 names "DNS txid" as the example of `token` correlation — but in mDNS the ID is 0x0000 in both my packets (RFC 6762 §18.1 requires it), so there is no token. The socket is a shared multicast group, so `socket` means nothing. And the response carries QDCOUNT=0 — RFC 6762 §6 forbids questions in responses — so there is literally nothing in the response echoing the request. Correlation must be a predicate over decoded records: does any record's owner name equal the queried name and its type match the qtype. Additionally, responses keep arriving from new devices indefinitely, so `broadcast` yielding a list has no completion condition, only quiescence.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a predicate correlation kind plus a quiescence terminator on `expect`:
{ "id":"gotResponses", "kind":"expect",
  "correlate": { "kind":"predicate",
                 "when":"any(capture.records, r -> r.name == inputs.service && r.type == consts.TYPE_PTR)" },
  "collect":   { "until":"quiescent", "quietMs":1500, "maxMs":6000, "maxItems":256,
                 "dedupeBy":"capture.records[0].name" } }
This also serves SSDP, LLDP, WS-Discovery and any other multicast-discovery protocol, so it is not a DNS special case.

gaps.what: The state model has no way to be driven by UNSOLICITED inbound traffic, which is how mDNS discovers that its own state is wrong.
gaps.why: §5's `implies` hangs off an `expect` step — a reply to a request you sent. In mDNS, name conflict is detected when some other host multicasts an authoritative record (flags 0x8400, as in my response capture) for the name you believe you own, with no request from you at all. Same for goodbye packets (TTL=0 withdrawing a record) and for duplicate-question suppression, where you must cancel your own pending send because you observed someone else ask the same question. There is no send to attach `implies` to, and §4's graph has no always-on node.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add standing observers to "model", live in every state, independent of the step graph:
"observers": [
  { "id":"conflictWatch", "listen":{ "port":5353, "group":"224.0.0.251" },
    "parse":"mdnsResponsePtr",
    "implies":[ { "when":"capture.records[*].name == store.myName && capture.records[*].rdata != store.myRdata",
                  "state":"renaming", "invalidate":["store.myName"] },
                { "when":"capture.records[*].ttl == 0",
                  "retract":"dev.mdns.peer(capture.records[*].name)" } ] } ]
This closes §5's admitted "state discovered by failure" gap for the connectionless case, and is the same primitive a subscription/push protocol (MQTT, SSE, CoAP observe) needs.

gaps.what: No modelling of probe/announce timing contracts, rate limits, or dedup windows — mDNS's core correctness rules are all temporal.
gaps.why: RFC 6762 requires: 3 probes 250 ms apart before claiming a name (§8.1); 2+ announcements 1 s apart (§8.3); at most 1 query/second per question with exponential backoff to 60 min (§5.2); shared-record responses delayed 20-120 ms randomly to avoid collision (§6.3); suppress your answer if you see an equivalent one within 500 ms. §5's `requires`:["probe"] proves a probe happened but carries no count, no spacing, and no "nothing contradicted you during the window" predicate. Note also the polarity inversion the graph must express: for a probe, TIMEOUT is success and MATCH is failure.
gaps.proposedFix:
Attach a temporal contract to a message and to a requires-edge:
"probe": { "validIn":["probing"],
           "repeat":{ "count":3, "intervalMs":250 },
           "successOn":"silence", "silenceMs":750 },
"mdnsResponsePtr": {
   "requires":[ { "message":"probe", "satisfiedBy":"silence", "withinMs":10000 } ],
   "rate":{ "minIntervalMs":1000, "backoff":"exponential", "maxIntervalMs":3600000 },
   "jitterMs":[20,120],
   "dedupWindowMs":500 }
This also covers §5's admitted retransmission/dedup gap (CoAP CON/ACK) with one primitive.

gaps.what: No per-state message VARIANTS: a legacy unicast query forces a different byte layout for the same logical response.
gaps.why: If the query's UDP source port is not 5353, RFC 6762 §6.7 requires the response to echo the question section (QDCOUNT=1, not the 0 in my capture), cap every TTL at 10 s (not 4500/120), and go unicast to the source port. Same message identity, different field list, selected by a property of the peer rather than by an input. §5 has validIn/requires/conflicts but no variant selection.
gaps.proposedFix:
Allow a message to declare ordered variants, first match wins, sharing an identity for validIn/requires/conflicts purposes:
"mdnsResponsePtr": {
  "variants": [
    { "id":"legacyUnicast", "when":"capture.srcPort != 5353",
      "overrides":{ "consts.TTL_SHARED":10, "consts.TTL_UNIQUE":10 },
      "layers":[ ... echoes the question ... ] },
    { "id":"multicast", "when":"true", "layers":[ ... ] } ] }
Same primitive covers protocol-version fallback and negotiated-capability downgrade generally.

gaps.what: The `udp` layer cannot express what an mDNS socket actually requires.
gaps.why: §2 says only "engine sets ports + broadcast flag". mDNS needs: join the 224.0.0.251 multicast group (IGMP), bind port 5353 with SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT so it coexists with the OS resolver, IP TTL exactly 255 (receivers check it), multicast loopback control, and a SOURCE port of 5353 — a querier that sends from an ephemeral port is classified by every responder as a legacy unicast client and gets the degraded response from the variant gap above. None of this is declarable; I wrote "ipTtl":255 in my document knowing §2 does not define it.
gaps.proposedFix:
Extend the udp layer schema:
{ "kind":"udp", "srcPort":5353, "dstPort":5353,
  "multicast":{ "group":"224.0.0.251", "join":true, "ipTtl":255,
                "loopback":false, "ifSelect":"adapter" },
  "reusePort":true }
Every field is a plain socket option, so this is configuration, not an engine change. Same shape serves SSDP (239.255.255.250:1900) and mDNS/IPv6 (ff02::fb).

gaps.what: The `dns` sugar layer is listed in §2 but has zero specification, and if it were specified to handle names and compression natively it would violate §7.
gaps.why: §2's table names `dns` as sugar that "expands to bytes + a transport intent". But everything hard about DNS — the label sequence, the 0xC0 backpointer, the absolute-offset table, the type-dependent RDATA — is exactly what does NOT survive expansion to the v0 `bytes` grammar, as the five blockers above establish. So either `dns` sugar is undefined (and this exercise had nothing to use), or it is a protocol-specific code path inside the engine, which §7 explicitly forbids: "If any of the three needs a code path specific to that protocol, the grammar has failed." The listing is currently a promissory note the grammar cannot honour.
gaps.proposedFix: Delete `dns` from the §2 sugar table and rebuild it as a pure macro over the fixed `bytes` grammar — legal only once `name`, `region`, `switch` and the offset table exist. Then `dns` expands to a normal field list a document author could have written by hand, and its expansion should be dumpable (a `--desugar` output) so the claim is auditable. Apply the same test to the other listed sugars: if a sugar cannot be expressed in the bytes grammar it is an engine special case wearing a layer's name.

gaps.what: Presumed-vs-confirmed state is modelled per MESSAGE, but mDNS produces N independent facts per message, each with its own TTL and its own flush semantics.
gaps.why: My response yields four facts (PTR, SRV, TXT, A) with TTLs 4500/120/4500/120 and cache-flush 0/1/1/1. The flush bit means "supersede prior records for this name+type, but delete the old ones after 1 second, not immediately" (RFC 6762 §10.2) — a two-stage confidence decay. TTL=0 in a goodbye packet is explicit retraction. RFC 6762 §5.2 requires refresh at 80/85/90/95% of TTL, so a fact is confirmed at receipt and decays to presumed as it ages. §5's effects.presume/confidence/ttl attaches one presumption to one message and cannot express any of this.
gaps.proposedFix:
Let `effects` emit per-decoded-element facts with expressions for ttl and confidence:
"effects": {
  "emitEach": { "over":"capture.records", "as":"r",
                "fact":"dev.mdns.record(r.name, r.type)",
                "value":"r.rdata",
                "ttl":"r.ttl | seconds",
                "confidence":"confirmed",
                "decayTo":{ "confidence":"likely", "atFraction":0.8 },
                "supersede":{ "when":"r.class & 0x8000", "graceMs":1000 },
                "retract":{ "when":"r.ttl == 0" } } }
